translations.text: James, servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes: greetings!
My brothers, count it all joy when you fall into trials of many kinds;
know that the testing of your faith produces patience,
and let patience have its perfect work, so that you may be perfect and wholly alive, lacking in nothing.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all generously and reproaches no one, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith and without doubting, for whoever doubts is like a wave of the sea, stirred up by the wind and tossed about.
Let that man not think that he will receive anything from God.
A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways.
Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation,
and the rich man in his humiliation, for he will pass away like the flower of the grass.
For the sun rose with its heat and withered the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance passed away. So too the rich man will wither away in his going.
Blessed is the man who endures trial, for once he has been proven he will receive the crown of life, which God promised to those who love him.
Let no one who is tempted say, "I am tempted by God," for God cannot be tempted by evil, and he tempts no one.
Instead, each person is tempted by his own desire, being drawn away and led astray.
Then desire conceives and gives birth to sin, and sin, once it is full-grown, gives birth to death.
Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers!
Every good thing given and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of light, with whom there is no change or shadow of turning.
By his own will he begot us by the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of beginning of his creatures.
So then, my beloved brothers, let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger.
For a man's anger does not work the righteousness of God.
Therefore put away all filthiness and the excess of wickedness, and with meekness receive the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
And be doers of the word, not only hearers who make fools of themselves.
If anyone is only a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like the man who looks at the face he was born with in a mirror.
For he looked at himself and went away, and at once forgot what he was like.
But whoever looked into the perfect law of freedom and stayed with it did not become a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work; that person will be blessed in his doing.
If anyone among you thinks that he is a servant of God, and does not bridle his tongue but deceives his own heart, this man's service is vain.
Service that is pure and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to look after orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself undefiled by this world.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with partiality.
For if a man with a gold ring and splendid clothing comes into your assembly, and a poor man in shabby clothing also comes in,
and you look to the one who wears the splendid clothing and say to him, "You sit here in a good place," and to the poor man you say, "You stand there," or, "Sit here below our feet,"
have you not made distinctions among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts of the heart?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen the poor of the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom that he promised to those who love him?
But you have dishonored the poor man. Is it not the rich who oppress you, and are they not the ones who drag you into court?
Is it not they who blaspheme the good name that has been called upon you?
If you fulfill the royal law according to the scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well.
But if you show partiality, you commit sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors of the law.
For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become liable for all of it.
For he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not kill." If you do not commit adultery but you kill, you have become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and so act as those who are to be judged by the law of freedom.
For judgment is without mercy for those who have not shown mercy; mercy boasts over judgment.
What profit is it, my brothers, if someone says, "I have faith," but does not have works? Can faith alone save him?
If a brother or sister is naked and lacking daily food,
and someone says to them, "Go in peace, be filled and be warmed," but does not give them what the body needs, what profit is it?
So also faith: if it does not have works, it is dead by itself.
But someone will say, "You have faith and I have works." Show me all [your] faith from your works [?], and I will show you my faith from my works.
You believe that God is one; you do well. The demons also believe, and they tremble before him.
Do you want to know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?
Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
Do you see that faith worked together with his works, and by works that faith was made perfect?
And the scripture was fulfilled that says, "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness," and he was called the friend of God.
Do you see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone?
Likewise also Rahab the harlot: was she not justified by works, for she received the messengers and sent them out by another way?
For as the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
Do not many of you become teachers, my brothers! Know that we shall receive the greater judgment.
For we all stumble greatly. Whoever does not stumble in word, he is a perfect man; he is able to bridle the whole body.
If we put bridles on a horse so that it obeys us, we turn it and its whole body.
Behold, even the ships, though very great and driven about by fierce winds, are turned by a small rudder wherever their steersman wishes to go.
So also the tongue is a small member and boasts greatly. Behold, how much material a small fire sets ablaze!

And the tongue likewise is a fire, an adornment of falsehood. The tongue is set among our members; it defiles the whole body and sets on fire the wheel of creation, and is itself set on fire by Gehenna.
For every kind of beasts and birds and creeping things and swimming creatures is tamed and has been tamed by humankind.
But no one is able to tame the human tongue, an unrestrainable evil, full of deadly poison.
For with it we bless God and the Father, and with the same we curse people, who are made in the likeness of God.
From the same mouth come forth blessing and cursing. It is not right, my beloved brothers, for this to be so.
Does sweet and bitter water gush forth from the same opening of a spring?
Can a fig tree, my brothers, bear olives, or a vine figs? Likewise no single spring can send forth both salt and sweet water.
Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show his works by good conduct in the meekness of wisdom.
But if you have bitter envy and strife in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth.
This is not the wisdom that comes down from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, devilish.
For where there is envy and strife, there is disorder and every evil deed.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, and then peaceable, kind, obedient, full of mercy and the fruit of good works, impartial and without duplicity.
For the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.
Where do wars and quarrels among you come from? Do they not come from your desires, which are at war in your members?
You desire and do not have; you kill and are envious and cannot obtain; you quarrel and fight and do not have, because you do not ask.
You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, so that you may spend it on your desires.
Harlots and adulterers, do you not know that love of this world is enmity toward God? So whoever wishes to be a friend of this world sets himself up as an enemy of God.
Or do you think that the scripture speaks in vain: "The spirit that dwells in us yearns to the point of envy"?
But he gives greater grace; therefore it says: "God crushes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
Submit to God and resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and make your hearts pure, you double-minded.
Be humbled, and weep and mourn. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.

Do not speak evil of one another, my brothers. Whoever speaks evil of a brother and judges his brother judges the law and condemns the law; and if you judge the law [?], you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
There is one lawgiver and judge, who is able to save and to destroy. Who are you, that you judge your neighbor?
Now you too, who say: "Today or tomorrow let us go to such and such a city, and spend a year there, and trade and make a profit" —
you who do not know what tomorrow will bring — for what is your life? You are like smoke, which appears for a little while and then vanishes.
Instead, you ought to say: "If the Lord wills, we shall live and do this or that."
But now you boast in your arrogance; all such boasting is evil.
Whoever knows the good thing to do and does not do it, for him it is sin.
Now then, you rich too, weep and wail over the miseries that are coming upon you.
Your wealth has rotted, and moths have eaten your clothing.
Your gold and your silver have rusted, and their rust will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.
Behold, the wages of the laborers who harvested your fields, which you have held back, cry out, and the cries of the reapers have reached the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.
You have lived in luxury on the earth and indulged yourselves. You have fattened your bodies as for a day of slaughter.
You have condemned and killed the righteous one, and he did not resist you.
Be patient, therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth and is patient over it until it receives the early and the late rain.
You too be patient; strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
Do not grumble against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Behold, the judge is standing at the doors.
Take as an example, my brothers, of suffering evil and of patience the prophets, who spoke in the name of the Lord.
Behold, we call blessed those who endured. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the end that the Lord brought about, for he is full of mercy and compassion.
Above all, my brothers, do not swear, neither by heaven, nor by earth, nor by any other oath; but let your yes be yes and your no be no, so that you do not fall into double-mindedness.
If anyone among you is in distress, let him pray; if anyone is cheerful, let him sing praise.
If anyone among you is sick, let him call the elders of the church, and let them pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
And the prayer of faith will save the sick man, and the Lord will raise him up. And if he has committed any sin, it will be forgiven him.
Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed, for the prayer of a righteous person, when it is assisted, has great power.
Elijah was a man like us, and he prayed a prayer that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months.
And again he prayed, and the sky gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
Brothers, if anyone among you strays from the truth and someone turns him back,
let them know that whoever turns a sinner back from the way of his error will save his own soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
